title: A Power-Liouville Hermite Orbit: Common Spectral Quantization of the Singular Sextic Oscillator and Fractional-Power Potentials
abstract: A singular sextic oscillator in the finite-Hermite biconfluent-Heun hierarchy generates an exact four-member power-Liouville Hermite orbit. Power coordinate transformations with the Liouville amplitude map the hierarchy member $N=4$ to four half-line Schrödinger spectral charts while preserving the physical regular-recessive Wronskian zero set under energy-coupling reparametrization. Two charts are the previously studied $x^{2/3}$ and inverse-square-root conditionally integrable potentials; the orbit embeds this known power-dual pair together with the singular sextic and linear-plus-quadratic charts. On the selected physical slice, the degree-five accessory compatibility obstruction vanishes identically, while the transformed Frobenius index reproduces both published fractional-power centrifugal coefficients. The common endpoint condition yields an exact discrete sequence of quartic Sturmian eigencouplings for the sextic oscillator. Independent two-sided shooting confirms representative eigencouplings and node counts. A matched large-action analysis further derives the first matched-endpoint correction within the leading Langer action and improves the Maslov-shifted effective-level approximation. The construction thus connects exact Hermite solvability, energy quantization, coupling quantization, and power duality within a single spectral orbit.
summary: This theoretical paper connects the spectral quantization of a singular sextic oscillator to fractional-power potentials by identifying a common 'power-Liouville Hermite orbit.' Using advanced techniques like coordinate transformations and semiclassical matching, the authors prove that these diverse potentials share an identical underlying quantization structure. This work provides a unified mathematical framework for understanding spectral properties across different physical models.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a deep mathematical connection between the spectral quantization of a singular sextic oscillator and various fractional-power potentials.
main_result: It demonstrates that these potentials share a common 'power-Liouville Hermite orbit,' characterized by an exact discrete sequence of quartic Sturmian eigencouplings for the sextic oscillator.
method: The analysis employs power-Liouville coordinate transformations and analyzes the invariance of the Wronskian zero set across different spectral charts derived from the biconfluent-Heun equation.
model_or_system: The core model is the singular sextic oscillator, analyzed within the framework of the biconfluent Heun equation. This system is shown to be spectrally equivalent to potentials like $x^{2/3}$ and inverse-square-root potentials.
key_observables: The exact discrete sequence of quartic Sturmian eigencouplings, the vanishing of the degree-five accessory compatibility obstruction, and the common physical zero set (Wronskian zero set).
important_parameters:
The index $N=4$ of the Hermite hierarchy, and the quantization parameter derived from the Frobenius index ($
u=5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on selecting a specific 'physical slice' and assumes that spectral equivalence is defined by the preservation of the physical zero set under reparametrization.

paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the spectral problem via the biconfluent Heun equation, then applying power-Liouville transformations to generate the orbit, and finally using advanced semiclassical methods (matched large-action analysis) to derive the precise quantization rules.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical connection established between multiple exactly solvable potentials via a single spectral orbit is highly relevant for understanding the underlying symmetries and quantization rules in quantum mechanics, applicable to systems modeled by complex differential equations.
